1.e4 c5 2.c3 Nf6.background: Its main line, 2...Nf6 3.e5 Nd5, is the one in current practice against the Alapin and can also arise when Black declines the Smith–Morra Gambit.

1.e4 c5 2.c3 Nf6 3.e5.strategy: Meets the attack on e4 by driving the knight away instead of defending the pawn, which the c3 pawn leaves without its natural defender. White gains space and a tempo; the price is an advanced pawn that has to stay supported against Black's pressure.

1.e4 c5 2.c3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5.strategy: The one square that keeps the knight active: it lands in the centre, presses on c3 and blocks the d-pawn's path, so White needs a pawn or a bishop move to challenge it. Black has spent two moves on this knight, so the game is about undermining e5 to justify it.
